messages:
mike: Seeing partial chat output over SSE — after the first data chunk the stream goes silent for ~5-10s, then the connection closes. Happening on 2 clients (iOS app and web). Request IDs I have: req-2000123001-aa7f, req-2000123456-bb9c
lisa: Sorry about that, can you share one full request id and the time window? Also which endpoint (sse/ws) + SDK or curl?
mike: Primary is SSE /v1/chat/stream. Sample req: req-2000123001-aa7f. Happened ~2026-03-15T22:13:05Z. Web client uses fetch/EventSource polyfill behind nginx.
ashok: Thanks — two common causes: (1) proxy/nginx buffering/coalescing, (2) client-side stream parser waiting for newline-prefixed events. Can you run curl against the hosted API from the flaky client network and capture raw bytes?
mike: I can. What's the exact curl you want?
ashok: Please run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-instruct-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Tell me a story"}]}'
```
and save output to a file: curl_out.bin
lisa: Also include a tcpdump/pcap if possible for the same timeframe so we can see TCP-level stalls (ngrep/tcpdump -w). If you can't share pcap publicly, upload to the Secure Debug Upload link I DM'd.
mike: Ran curl, saved. A snippet of the chunked output (raw, with colon heartbeats removed) looks like:
```
data: {"id":"c1","delta":"Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a"

# silence for 6s
```
kevin: That pattern (first data then silence) is classic proxy buffering — some edge/proxy will buffer until a size/timeout threshold then flush. Can you paste your nginx config (proxy_buffering, proxy_request_buffering) and any Fastly/Cloudflare workers in front?
mike: We're on a CDN + nginx origin. proxy_buffering off already, but we have an edge worker rewriting headers. Edge worker script uploaded to the customer portal (upload id 9876).
ashok: Next steps for us: please attach the curl_out.bin, the pcap (tcpdump), and the API request id(s) to this thread. We'll run server-side traces for req-2000123001-aa7f and req-2000123456-bb9c. Also try a direct curl from a digitalocean droplet (no CDN/nginx) to see if replica reproduces — that isolates client vs edge.
lisa: FYI: deploy-bot reports a recent streaming kernel tweak last week — @ashok can check if the runtime emitted any backpressure logs around those req ids.
deploy-bot: Runtime deploy rwd-runtime-v2.4.1 rolled 2026-03-12T03:00:00Z — no hard failures reported.
ashok: On our side I'll request the server access logs and internal trace for the specific request ids. If you can also capture the browser Console logs (EventSource errors) that helps. A helpful debug bundle includes: curl_out.bin, pcap, nginx conf, browser_console.txt, and exact request payloads.
mike: Uploading files now to the DM link and adding this thread link. One more question: is there a known SSE keepalive format you expect? Our polyfill strips colon heartbeats and maybe eats the following newline.
ashok: Preferred pattern: server sends `:\n` (colon + LF) every ~15s as a heartbeat. Also each data event should be terminated by a double newline. If polyfill removes the blank line, the client may wait for termination. For reproducible test, try sending `--data-binary $'\n'` after first chunk to force flush from your worker.
lisa: Thanks — will coordinate with infra (kevin) and engineering. We'll follow up in 24h with trace results. :thumbsup:
kevin: Quick tip: if you can reproduce with `nc` to our endpoint and see the same behavior, paste the transcript. That'll speed triage.
mike: Understood — thanks everyone. I'll post uploads and the nc transcript when done.
